Figure 4:Case study on physical context and self-teacher generation.From a swing-set reference,PhysOPSDconstructs dual-level drafts (𝐝dense,𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}},\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}}) across paired variants varying only in initial angular velocity (0.120.12vs.1.7​rad/s1.7\text{ rad/s}).
Conditioned on these drafts, the self-teacher faithfully synthesizes the corresponding motion dynamics.

Figure 5:Qualitative results ofPhysOPSD. More results are shown inFigures14,15,16and17.
Figure 6:Privilege context analysis.Executable coding drafts yield superior physical adherence over text and real videos.

Figure 7:Structured physical privilege analysis.Both (Left) the stepped dual-level hierarchy and (Right) parameter-controlled paired variations consistently yield superior physical adherence over their uncoupled counterparts.
Figure 8:Data scaling analysis.PhysOPSDdelivers physical improvements even in low-data regimes and scales steadily.

Figure 11:Case study ofPhysOPSDon rigid-body and contact dynamics.
(Left)Pendulum wave: perturbing the damping rate (0.0180.018vs.1.4​s−11.4\text{ s}^{-1}) yields sustained wave oscillationsvs.rapid kinetic decay.
(Right)Domino cascade: varying gravitational acceleration (0.9810.981vs.9.81​m/s29.81\text{ m/s}^{2}) alters the collapse speed from sluggish, incomplete toppling to rapid, sequential falling.

Figure 12:Case study ofPhysOPSDon elastic and deformable solid mechanics. (Left)Transverse spring wave: modulating transverse coupling stiffness (0.50.5vs.8​N/m8\text{ N/m}) shifts dynamic response from localized dispersion to cohesive wave propagation.
(Right)Sponge compression: increasing actuator displacement (88vs.24​mm24\text{ mm}) drives the deformation from moderate compaction to severe, non-linear flattening.

Figure 13:Case study ofPhysOPSDon fluid dynamics. (Left)Fluid drainage: altering the container outlet radius (1.81.8vs.5.5​mm5.5\text{ mm}) controls the discharge flux from a thin, laminar stream to a high-volume outflow. (Right)Coffee stirring: varying spoon angular velocity (33vs.14​rad/s14\text{ rad/s}) transitions the fluid motion from a smooth spiral vortex to vigorous turbulent mixing and foam dispersion.
